pr_title: storage: add TBI optimization to MVCCClearTimeRange and RevertRange
pr_body:
This change adds an option to enable a TBI optimization for the
RevertRange command.

The optimization affects the following places:

- We use a TBI to seek to the start key in an MVCCClearTimeRange.

- Once we hit a key that does not fall in our (startTime, endTime] and
  we Clear the buffered keys, we use the TBI to potentially jump over a
  swath of irrelevant keys and rely on it to get us to the next key in our
  time range.

Fixes: #57415

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/58039)
I still need to add tests and clean the code a little, but wanted to get it out for an early pass just to make sure this is the approach we have in mind.

> I don't understand why we pass both StartTime, EndTime in MVCCIncrementalIterOptions, and the MinTimestampHint, MaxTimestampHint in IterOptions. This has come up before, and seeing this code really suggests we should do that (minor) cleanup first since we are plumbing these things through many layers, e.g. starting in export.go to ExportMVCCToSst to pebbleExportToSst. It seems to me we could pass in just the values in MVCCIncrementalIterOptions and inside NewMVCCIncrementalIterator set the MinTimestampHint, MaxTimestampHint appropriately.

I believe the existence of these fields is used as a way of conveying to the MVCCIncIterator whether or not we should enable the TBI. I'm +1 on explicitly plumbing a bool rather than these timestamps, I'll send out a separate PR for that.

>Is there a reason to add another iterator instead of changing MVCCIncrementalIterator to support this pattern.

@sumeerbhola this is what I was initially hoping for but I'm having a hard time wrapping my head around how this would end up looking. One strawman I have is as follows:

1. Initialize IncIter i.
2. i.SeekGE() to find the start key.
3. Buffer Clear(). 
4. Have a loop that invokes i.NextVersion() which moves the non-TBI iter to Next(), and returns the next version of the current key even if it is outside (startTime, endTime].
           - If it is within the time range then buffer for Clear.
           - If it is outside the time range update the stats with the uncovered key, flush the buffered Clear's, and break.
           - If it is not the next version of the current key, but the next new key, then break.
5. i.ModifiedAdvance() which is the same as i.advance() (https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/master/pkg/storage/mvcc_incremental_iterator.go#L273) but returns whether or not any keys were skipped. After this call, the IncIter will be pointing at the next key in (startTime, endTime] and may have used the TBI to arrive there.
          - If i.ModifiedAdvance() indicates that keys were skipped, we flush the current buffered Clear's.
6. Repeat from step 3.

issue_context.title: storage: leverage time bound iterators in MVCCClearTimeRange
issue_context.body:
As part of cluster-to-cluster streaming, the ingestion job will rollback to the latest timestamp at which we can offer a consistent view of the ingested data. It does so by issuing a `RevertRange` request, which is powered by `MVCCClearTimeRange`. This is currently an O(cluster size) operation.

We expect that the time range we want to clear is much smaller than the time range of all the data in the cluster. So, a time-bound iterator should enable dramatic performance improvements of such RevertRange requests.
